new_indicators.definition: Number of awards whose percentage a programme reduced in a period because of a negative factor (unreasonable reporting delay, culpability, interference with internal reporting); breakdown item= gives the reason.

new_indicators.name: Enforcement actions to protect whistleblowers
new_indicators.definition: Enforcement actions an agency brought in a period or to date against entities or people for impeding whistleblowers from reporting (e.g. SEC Rule 21F-17, restrictive agreements) or for retaliating against them; breakdown item= (impeding, retaliation).

new_indicators.name: Share of eligible awards given the maximum-award presumption

new_indicators.notes: proposed by extract-whistleblowing-usa9 (SEC FY2024 report: presumption applied about 90% of the time where the maximum award would be $5 million or less).

new_indicators.name: Preliminary determinations on award claims
new_indicators.definition: Preliminary decisions a programme issued on award claims in a period, before the final order, as the source counts them; breakdown item= says which: award_recommended, denial_recommended, preliminary_summary_dispositions (summary preliminary denials) or all. Counts determinations or claims, not final orders.

ledger.contains: SEC OWB 2020 Annual Report to Congress (16 Nov 2020, 48 pp.; cover, photos and maps are images; all tables are text): message (FY2020 $175 million to 39; cumulative $562 million to 106; sanctions >$2.7 billion, >$1.5 billion disgorgement, >$850 million returned; FY2020 = 31% of dollars and 37% of recipients; 197 Final Orders; 315 claims to Preliminary Determination; tips 6,911 from 78 foreign countries; hotline 2,850 and 26,900 since 2011), staffing, top 10 awards chart (7 per-award and 3 per-covered-action pre-FY2020 entries added as month-dated cases, flagged as overlapping; FY2020 entries already recorded), 33 FY2020 award descriptions (already recorded, with splits), award factors (32 Covered Actions, >90% significance, 72% assistance, 81% insiders internal, 40% outsiders, 2 reduced for delay), 105 NoCAs, process and deadlines (record and meeting requests 30 days; others already in rules), profiles since inception (87 Covered Actions, 71/29 caused/contributed, 68% insiders and 84% of them internal, defendants 45/33/22 by type, 12 joint matters, 10 related-action and 19 foreign recipients), anti-retaliation and 21F-17 actions to date (3 and 12), tips (by year FY2012-FY2019 and category shares added; category chart and 1,689 uncategorised already recorded and add to 6,911; 130 countries since inception), >1,100 tracked matters, 2020 rule amendments (event already recorded; TCR 30-day waiver, DPA/NPA 90-day window and the 3-frivolous-application bar added as rules; 75% of awards historically $5 million or less), Fund table (all lines added; adds up), Appendix A FY2017-FY2019 by category added (ICO year assignment flagged), Appendix B 54 states and territories added (sum 4,087 matches), Appendix C (already recorded except Curaçao, added; now 78 countries summing to 751). Collector's Coffee amended complaint added as an event. Words-only figures ("two-thirds", "all of the awards", "nearly all") not recorded.

SEC OWB 2021 Annual Report to Congress (15 Nov 2021, 44 pp.; maps on pp. 31 and 39-40 are images; Appendix C country table already recorded): message (cumulative >$1.1 billion to 214 and sanctions nearly $5 billion / disgorgement >$3.1 billion / >$1.3 billion returned; FY2011-FY2020 $562 million to 106; FY2021 $564 million to 108; 318 Final Orders; 354 claims to Preliminary Determination or Summary Disposition; tips >12,200 from 99 foreign countries; hotline 2,600 calls, 29,500 since 2011; two protection actions; two bars), staffing, process and deadlines (record request 30 days; summary disposition 15 and 30 days; other deadlines already in rules), 2020 amendments, top 10 awards chart (6 per-award and 4 per-covered-action entries added as month-dated cases, flagged as overlapping; FY2021 entries already recorded), five largest FY2021 awards (already recorded; splits and factors as suggested corrections), 150 NoCAs, 86 Covered Actions, award factor statistics (46% at maximum before amendments, 89% presumption, 7 delay matters, 2 culpability, award % distribution 85/10/5, 4 DPAs/NPAs >$117 million, 8 independent-analysis awards, 69 PSDs / 31 final), profiles (20% abroad, 56/44 caused/contributed, 60% insiders, >75% of them reported internally, six joint matters, 17 related-action recipients), anti-retaliation and 21F-17 actions (4 and 14 to date; GPB, Guggenheim, Collector's Coffee as events), tips (12,210 and categories already recorded; category shares added; tips by year chart FY2012-FY2020 added (FY2021 already recorded); Appendix A FY2018-FY2020 by category added (FY2018 ICO bar unlabelled); Appendix B 53 states and territories added (sum 6,453 vs "approximately 6,470"); 133 countries since inception), >1,300 tracked matters, Fund table (all lines; adds up to $144,442,133.88, while the FY2022 report gives an opening balance of $144,441,949.35), Notable cases added: Rel. 92542, 90350, bars Rel. 92969 and 93145. Not recorded: 46 press releases (outreach, out of scope), delay range in words, the template placeholder "approximately $? million to ? individuals" on p. 10.

SEC OWB results for FY2022 (annual report, 15 Nov 2022, 9 pp.; top-five chart p. 3, tips-by-year chart p. 5 and category chart p. 6 are images, read by OCR): awards (about $229 million in 103 awards; cumulative >$1.3 billion in 328 awards), sanctions in whistleblower cases (>$6.3 billion, of which >$4.0 billion disgorgement and interest and >$1.5 billion returned to investors), awards in 70 Covered Actions and 8 related actions, five noteworthy matters (Rel. 95384 award and 95486 denial already recorded; Rel. 94789, 94736 and 94860 added as cases without amounts), top five awards (already recorded; per-whistleblower splits given as suggested corrections), presumption applied to more than 90% of awards, 14 Covered Actions with several independent whistleblowers, awards reduced (8 delay, 3 culpability), 2022 rule amendments (event already recorded), tips (12,322 and category chart already recorded; chart of tips by year FY2012-FY2021 and category shares added; categories plus "almost 3,000" uncategorised = about 12,325, consistent with the total), top countries and states named by rank only, anti-impeding actions (16 to date, 2 in FY2022; Brink's, a co-founder and Collector's Coffee described without penalty amounts; Brink's $75,000 liquidated-damages clause is not a programme figure), Fund table (all lines; adds up), $300 million replenishment trigger (rule already recorded), hotline calls >2,500. Dated anti-impeding/retaliation actions added as events.

SEC OWB Annual Report to Congress FY2023 (14 Nov 2023, 9 pp.; top-five chart p. 3 and category chart p. 6 are images, checked by OCR): awards (nearly $600 million to 68 individuals; cumulative >$1.9 billion to 397; awards in 40 Covered Actions; six related-action awards), five noteworthy awards and top five chart (cases already recorded; two noteworthy awards without amounts, Rel. 96178 and 96076, added as cases), presumption applied nearly 90%, awards reduced (5 delay, 1 culpability), tips 18,354 with a chart of tips by year FY2012-FY2022 (added), category shares (added) and category chart (already recorded: the ten categories plus 4,591 uncategorised sum to 18,345, 9 fewer than the 18,354 total; difference unexplained in the source), top countries and states by rank only, anti-impeding and anti-retaliation actions (5 in FY2023, 21 and 5 to date), D.E. Already recorded: 644 denial and bar rows. Added: the 2 denial rows that were missing (May 12, 2014 multiple-denial order owb-multiple-final-051214; Aug. 12, 2022 Rel. 95486) and the denial part of 10 "Award and Denial" rows whose order PDF is not stored (one row each, at least one denial; number not on the list). Non-award items: the Feb 2022 rule proposal and the Sept 2021 two-person bar added as events; the statements, the Aug 2022 and Sept 2020 rule items and the staff change were already covered by events. The stored page lists no award press release after April 2025. The 73 items on page 2 (older releases) are not in this document; the 2021 list covers them.
